name: Mahamaya Specialized Pharmacology Intelligence — V5.40H Hematology • Anemia • Hematinics Lab
global_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. V5.40G adds a dedicated Antifungal • Antiviral • Antiparasitic Intelligence Lab while retaining all earlier specialized labs. Exact organism/species, disease site/severity, resistance/susceptibility, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy, age/weight, G6PD status, interactions and current guideline/regulatory label must be verified. HIV/HBV/HCV, invasive fungal disease, severe malaria and complex tissue parasitoses remain regimen- and specialist-controlled.

labs.title: Antihypertensive Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Classification → RAAS / CCB / diuretics / sympathetic systems → generics → dose/formulation → compelling-context lens → evidence verification
labs.scientific_boundary: This is a pharmacology/research atlas, not an automatic antihypertensive selector. “First-line/core”, CKD, pregnancy, resistant-HTN and emergency tags are learning/context lenses. Actual choice requires confirmed BP phenotype, comorbidities, kidney function/electrolytes, pregnancy status, interactions and the current guideline/label.

classification_notes.first_line: 2025 AHA/ACC identifies ACE inhibitors, ARBs, long-acting dihydropyridine CCBs and thiazide-type diuretics as major classes used to initiate treatment; individualized combinations and comorbidities determine selection.
classification_notes.raas: ACEi and ARB are alternative RAAS-blocking strategies; routine dual RAAS blockade is generally avoided because of renal/hyperkalemia risk.
classification_notes.resistant: Resistant hypertension requires confirmation of adherence/measurement, secondary-cause review and rational combination therapy; MRA therapy is a key pharmacologic teaching category.
classification_notes.emergency: Hypertensive emergency is defined by severe BP elevation with acute target-organ injury; IV agent choice and rate of BP reduction are syndrome-specific and monitored-setting decisions.

classes.name: ACE inhibitors (ACEi)
classes.mechanism: Reduce angiotensin II formation and bradykinin breakdown
classes.role_note: Core RAAS-blocking class; common foundational option when indicated. ACEi and ARB should not be combined routinely.

classes.name: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARB)
classes.mechanism: Block angiotensin II signaling at AT1 receptor
classes.role_note: Core RAAS-blocking class; often used when ACEi cough/angioedema context makes ACEi unsuitable.

classes.name: Long-acting dihydropyridine CCBs
classes.mechanism: Reduce vascular smooth-muscle calcium entry and arteriolar resistance
classes.role_note: Core BP-lowering class with strong vasodilator effect; edema is a common class effect.

classes.name: Non-dihydropyridine CCBs
classes.mechanism: Reduce AV-node conduction and myocardial/vascular calcium entry
classes.role_note: Useful when rate control is also desired; not interchangeable with DHP-CCBs.

classes.name: Thiazide / thiazide-like diuretics
classes.mechanism: Promote natriuresis at distal convoluted tubule
classes.role_note: Core hypertension class; chlorthalidone/indapamide are longer acting thiazide-like options.

classes.name: Loop diuretics
classes.mechanism: Potent natriuresis in thick ascending limb
classes.role_note: More useful for volume overload/heart failure/advanced CKD than uncomplicated hypertension.

classes.name: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
classes.mechanism: Block aldosterone signaling and sodium retention
classes.role_note: High-yield add-on class in resistant hypertension and selected heart-failure contexts; potassium/renal monitoring is central.

classes.name: Epithelial sodium-channel blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce sodium reabsorption in collecting duct
classes.role_note: Potassium-sparing diuretics; usually adjunctive rather than first-line monotherapy.

classes.name: β1-selective beta blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce heart rate, contractility and renin release
classes.role_note: Not universal first-line hypertension therapy, but important with CAD/post-MI, tachyarrhythmia and selected HF contexts.

classes.name: Combined α/β blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce sympathetic vascular tone and cardiac adrenergic drive
classes.role_note: Labetalol is important in pregnancy/emergency contexts; carvedilol is a heart-failure/CAD drug with BP effects.

classes.name: Non-selective beta blockers
classes.mechanism: Block β1 and β2 adrenergic receptors
classes.role_note: Useful for selected compelling indications; bronchospasm risk matters.

classes.name: α1-adrenergic blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce peripheral vascular α1-mediated tone
classes.role_note: Usually add-on therapy; can help concomitant BPH but orthostatic hypotension is important.

classes.name: Central sympatholytics / α2 agonists
classes.mechanism: Reduce central sympathetic outflow
classes.role_note: Generally later-line; rebound hypertension is important with abrupt clonidine withdrawal.

classes.name: Direct arteriolar vasodilators
classes.mechanism: Directly relax arteriolar smooth muscle
classes.role_note: Hydralazine/minoxidil are later-line agents; reflex tachycardia and fluid retention often require companion therapy.

classes.name: Direct renin inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Suppresses RAAS at renin step
classes.role_note: Aliskiren is a specialist/alternative RAAS agent; combination restrictions with ACEi/ARB are important in selected populations.

classes.name: Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI)
classes.mechanism: AT1 blockade plus neprilysin inhibition
classes.role_note: Primarily a heart-failure therapy with BP-lowering effect; not a routine hypertension-first-line class.

classes.name: IV antihypertensive / hypertensive-emergency agents
classes.mechanism: Rapid titratable hemodynamic control in monitored settings
classes.role_note: Hospital/ICU category only. Agent choice depends on acute target-organ injury, aortic syndrome, ACS, pregnancy, pulmonary edema, renal function and local protocol.

labs.title: Antidiabetic Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Classification → glucose physiology target → oral/injectable/insulin families → generics/formulations → cardiorenal/weight lenses → evidence verification
labs.scientific_boundary: This lab is a pharmacology and evidence-navigation workspace, not an automatic glucose-lowering regimen generator. Comorbidity lenses (ASCVD, HF, CKD, weight, hypoglycemia) are research prompts; treatment must integrate diabetes type, HbA1c/glucose pattern, symptoms, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy, age/frailty, cost/access and current label/guideline.

classification_notes.physiology: Drug classes can be understood by dominant physiology: hepatic glucose output/insulin sensitivity, pancreatic insulin secretion, incretin signaling, renal glucose transport, intestinal carbohydrate absorption and exogenous insulin replacement.
classification_notes.cardiorenal: Modern T2D therapy is not ranked only by HbA1c. SGLT2 inhibitors and selected GLP-1–based therapies have important cardiorenal/weight roles in appropriate patients.
classification_notes.insulin: Insulin is mandatory replacement in type 1 diabetes and may be needed in type 2 diabetes for marked hyperglycemia, catabolic symptoms, acute illness or progressive beta-cell failure.
classification_notes.hypoglycemia: Insulin and secretagogues carry greater hypoglycemia risk than metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, DPP-4 inhibitors, TZDs and GLP-1–based therapies when used without insulin/secretagogue.

classes.name: Biguanide
classes.mechanism: Suppresses hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity
classes.role_note: Metformin-centered foundational class in many T2D pathways; renal tolerance and GI/B12 issues matter.

classes.name: Sulfonylureas
classes.mechanism: Close β-cell KATP channels → insulin release
classes.role_note: Potent, inexpensive insulin secretagogues; hypoglycemia and weight gain are major selection trade-offs.

classes.name: Meglitinides / glinides
classes.mechanism: Short-acting KATP-channel closure → meal-time insulin release
classes.role_note: Meal-time secretagogues with shorter action than sulfonylureas.

classes.name: Thiazolidinediones (TZD)
classes.mechanism: Increase insulin sensitivity through nuclear transcription effects
classes.role_note: Insulin-sensitizing class; edema/HF, fractures and weight effects shape use.

classes.name: α-glucosidase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Delay intestinal carbohydrate digestion/absorption
classes.role_note: Postprandial-focused agents; gastrointestinal adverse effects are common.

classes.name: DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins)
classes.mechanism: Prolong endogenous GLP-1/GIP action
classes.role_note: Generally weight-neutral, low-hypoglycemia oral incretin enhancers; renal dosing differs by molecule.

classes.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Increase urinary glucose excretion and alter renal-cardiorenal physiology
classes.role_note: Glucose-lowering plus important HF/CKD benefits for selected patients; eGFR and acute illness/ketosis precautions matter.

classes.name: Dual SGLT1/SGLT2 inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Reduces intestinal glucose absorption and renal glucose reabsorption
classes.role_note: Specialized dual transporter inhibition; regulatory indications vary by country.

classes.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
classes.mechanism: Enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon, slow gastric emptying and increase satiety
classes.role_note: High-efficacy incretin class with substantial weight and cardiometabolic effects depending agent.

classes.name: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist
classes.mechanism: Dual incretin-receptor agonism
classes.role_note: Very high glycemic and weight efficacy; GI effects and titration are central.

classes.name: Amylin analog
classes.mechanism: Slows gastric emptying, suppresses postprandial glucagon and increases satiety
classes.role_note: Adjunct to mealtime insulin in selected patients; insulin-dose coordination is essential.

classes.name: Other oral glucose-lowering agents
classes.mechanism: Miscellaneous central/bile-acid/mitochondrial mechanisms
classes.role_note: Less commonly used/region-specific oral agents that remain pharmacologically relevant.

classes.name: Rapid / ultra-rapid insulin analogs
classes.mechanism: Exogenous insulin replacement with rapid prandial kinetics
classes.role_note: Prandial insulin category; dosing is carbohydrate/glucose/insulin-sensitivity dependent rather than a universal fixed dose.

classes.name: Short-acting human insulin
classes.mechanism: Exogenous insulin replacement with slower prandial kinetics than analogs
classes.role_note: Regular human insulin; also used IV in specific acute-care protocols.

classes.name: Intermediate-acting insulin
classes.mechanism: Basal/intermediate insulin replacement
classes.role_note: NPH has pronounced peak and more hypoglycemia variability than long-acting analogs.

classes.name: Long / ultra-long basal insulin analogs
classes.mechanism: Relatively peakless basal insulin replacement
classes.role_note: Basal insulin category for T1D and advanced T2D; titration is individualized.

classes.name: Premixed insulin formulations
classes.mechanism: Fixed basal/prandial insulin proportions
classes.role_note: Simplifies injection schedule but reduces flexibility; meal consistency matters.

classes.name: Fixed-dose / fixed-ratio diabetes combinations
classes.mechanism: Combines complementary pharmacologic pathways
classes.role_note: Common combination patterns can reduce pill/injection burden; exact strength and suitability are product-specific.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 500 mg once or twice daily with food; titrate gradually.

labs.title: Thyroid Drugs Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Hypothyroid replacement → hyperthyroid synthesis/release blockers → symptom control → thyroid storm → radioiodine → orbitopathy → precision oncology
labs.scientific_boundary: This lab separates thyroid pharmacology by disease mechanism. Replacement, antithyroid, thyroid-storm, pregnancy, orbitopathy and oncology therapies are not interchangeable. Exact drug choice/dose must be based on thyroid diagnosis, TSH/free T4/T3 pattern, etiology (Graves/toxic nodule/thyroiditis), pregnancy status, cardiac/liver risk and current ATA/product guidance.

classification_notes.hypothyroid: Levothyroxine remains standard replacement for primary hypothyroidism; dose is individualized by age, weight, pregnancy, cardiac disease and TSH response.
classification_notes.hyperthyroid: Thionamides block new hormone synthesis and are useful in Graves disease; they do not treat hormone leakage from thyroiditis. Beta blockers control symptoms but do not correct hormone production.
classification_notes.storm: Thyroid storm is a multimodal emergency: adrenergic control + synthesis blockade + iodide after thionamide + glucocorticoid/supportive care, with syndrome-specific protocol.
classification_notes.pregnancy: Pregnancy management is specialized. ATA updated its preconception/pregnancy/postpartum guideline in 2026; antithyroid and levothyroxine decisions should use that current guidance.

classes.name: T4 replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces endogenous thyroxine; peripheral conversion supplies T3
classes.target: Thyroid hormone receptors after T4→T3 conversion
classes.role_note: Levothyroxine is standard replacement therapy for primary hypothyroidism; dose is TSH/clinical-context guided.

classes.name: T3 / combination thyroid hormone
classes.mechanism: Provides liothyronine directly or T4/T3 combination
classes.role_note: Specialist/selected use rather than routine first-line replacement.

classes.name: Desiccated thyroid extract
classes.mechanism: Animal-derived T4/T3-containing preparation
classes.role_note: Not standard first-line therapy; content ratio differs from human physiology and products require careful standardization.

classes.name: Thionamide antithyroid drugs
classes.mechanism: Inhibit thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4→T3 conversion
classes.role_note: Core medication class for Graves hyperthyroidism; methimazole is usually preferred outside specific pregnancy/thyroid-storm contexts.

classes.name: Beta blockers for thyrotoxicosis
classes.mechanism: Control adrenergic symptoms; propranolol at higher doses also reduces T4→T3 conversion
classes.role_note: Symptom-control adjunct; does not treat the underlying hormone overproduction.

classes.name: Inorganic iodide / hormone-release blockade
classes.mechanism: Acute Wolff–Chaikoff effect and inhibition of thyroid hormone release
classes.role_note: Short-term adjunct in thyroid storm/preoperative settings; sequencing after thionamide matters in storm protocols.

classes.name: Radioactive iodine (I-131)
classes.mechanism: Thyroid-selective beta radiation after iodide uptake
classes.role_note: Definitive therapy for selected Graves/toxic nodular disease; contraindications and radiation precautions are essential.

classes.name: Thyroid-storm / severe thyrotoxicosis adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Reduce peripheral conversion, enterohepatic recycling or hormone release
classes.role_note: ICU-level multimodal therapy; components are adjuncts and sequence/timing are protocol-driven.

classes.name: Graves orbitopathy pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Immunomodulation / IGF-1R pathway inhibition
classes.role_note: Specialist ophthalmology/endocrinology therapy based on activity/severity and local availability.

classes.name: Rare/specialist hormone-release inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Reduce thyroid hormone release/iodide uptake in selected refractory or amiodarone contexts
classes.role_note: Rare specialist agents; toxicity and availability limit routine use.

classes.name: RAI-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer targeted therapy
classes.mechanism: Inhibit VEGFR/RET and other oncogenic kinases
classes.role_note: Oncology-level systemic therapy for progressive RAI-refractory disease; mutation and toxicity profiles guide selection.

classes.name: Medullary thyroid cancer targeted therapy
classes.mechanism: Inhibit RET/VEGFR/MET or selective RET signaling
classes.role_note: Advanced medullary thyroid cancer therapy; RET mutation status increasingly matters.

classes.name: Anaplastic thyroid cancer / precision therapy
classes.mechanism: Target BRAF/MEK or actionable molecular drivers
classes.role_note: Urgent multidisciplinary oncology care; targeted options depend on rapid molecular profiling.

drugs.dose_example: Healthy younger adults needing full replacement often require ~1.6 microgram/kg/day; start lower in older/cardiac patients and titrate by TSH.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH (and free T4 in selected contexts), adherence/timing; absorption interactions with iron/calcium/antacids.

labs.title: Acid-Peptic / Anti-ulcer Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Antacids → alginates → H2RA → PPI → P-CAB → mucosal protection → NSAID-ulcer prevention → H. pylori eradication → selected motility/reflux adjuncts
labs.scientific_boundary: This is a pharmacology/research atlas, not an automatic GERD/ulcer prescription. Dyspepsia, GERD, peptic ulcer, H. pylori infection, NSAID injury, bleeding and alarm symptoms are different clinical problems. Exact regimen requires confirmed indication, H. pylori strategy, interacting medicines, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status, bleeding risk and current guideline/label.

classification_notes.ppi: PPIs are the core potent acid-suppression class for many GERD/ulcer indications. ACG GERD guidance emphasizes appropriate indication and an empiric PPI trial for classic symptoms, with reassessment rather than indefinite unreviewed use.
classification_notes.hpylori: ACG 2024 recommends optimized 14-day bismuth quadruple therapy as a preferred empiric regimen in many treatment-naïve adults when antibiotic susceptibility is unknown; clarithromycin-containing therapy should not be used empirically without appropriate susceptibility context.
classification_notes.nsaid_ulcer: For NSAID-associated peptic ulcer, guidelines emphasize stopping/reducing the NSAID when possible and using acid-suppression/gastroprotection according to risk and indication.
classification_notes.prokinetic: Prokinetics and baclofen are adjunct/specialist categories, not substitutes for correct diagnosis or core acid-suppression/eradication therapy.

classes.name: Antacids / gastric acid neutralizers
classes.mechanism: Directly neutralize luminal gastric acid; some salts also bind bile acids/pepsin
classes.role_note: Rapid symptom-relief category; short acting and formulation-specific. Does not heal all acid-peptic disease or eradicate H. pylori.

classes.name: Alginate / reflux-suppressant raft formulations
classes.mechanism: Forms a low-density raft/barrier over gastric contents and may reduce post-prandial reflux
classes.role_note: Mechanical reflux-suppression adjunct; composition and antacid content vary by product.

classes.name: Histamine-2 receptor antagonists (H2RA)
classes.mechanism: Reversibly block histamine H2 receptors on parietal cells and reduce basal/nocturnal acid secretion
classes.role_note: Acid-suppressive class with faster onset than PPIs but less potent sustained suppression; tachyphylaxis can occur with continuous use.

classes.name: Proton-pump inhibitors (PPI)
classes.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibit active gastric H+/K+-ATPase pumps after activation in acidic canaliculi
classes.role_note: Core potent acid-suppression class. Timing, duration, CYP interactions and long-term indication review are important research points.

classes.name: Potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CAB)
classes.mechanism: Competitively and reversibly inhibit K+ binding at gastric H+/K+-ATPase
classes.role_note: Rapid, potent acid suppression; approved indications and availability vary by jurisdiction.

classes.name: Sucralfate / mucosal barrier therapy
classes.mechanism: Polymerizes in acid and adheres to ulcerated mucosa, creating a protective barrier
classes.role_note: Mucosal-protective rather than systemic acid-suppression therapy; drug-binding interactions and administration separation matter.

classes.name: Bismuth compounds
classes.mechanism: Mucosal coating plus local antimicrobial/anti-secretory effects depending salt
classes.role_note: Bismuth salts have distinct formulations and salicylate content; an important component of H. pylori bismuth quadruple therapy.

classes.name: Prostaglandin E1 analogue gastroprotection
classes.mechanism: Replaces prostaglandin-mediated mucus/bicarbonate support and reduces acid secretion
classes.role_note: Misoprostol is an NSAID-ulcer prevention option but has dose-limiting GI effects and major pregnancy/uterotonic implications.

classes.name: H. pylori optimized bismuth quadruple regimen
classes.mechanism: Combines potent acid suppression with bismuth + tetracycline + nitroimidazole antimicrobial therapy
classes.role_note: Regimen-level learning record; resistance history, prior antibiotics, allergy, local availability and test-of-cure matter.

classes.name: H. pylori rifabutin-based triple regimen
classes.mechanism: Acid suppression + high-dose amoxicillin + rifabutin-based eradication strategy
classes.role_note: Specialized eradication strategy; exact co-formulation/regimen should follow current guideline/label.

classes.name: Vonoprazan-based H. pylori dual/triple regimens
classes.mechanism: P-CAB acid suppression combined with amoxicillin ± clarithromycin
classes.role_note: Current labeled regimens exist in some jurisdictions; clarithromycin use should respect susceptibility/resistance guidance.

classes.name: Prokinetic / upper-GI motility adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Enhance gastric emptying or upper-GI motility through dopamine/5-HT/cholinergic pathways
classes.role_note: Not primary acid-suppression drugs. Benefit and safety are indication-specific; QT and extrapyramidal risks are important for some agents.

classes.name: GABA-B reflux-event modulator (selected refractory context)
classes.mechanism: Reduces transient lower oesophageal sphincter relaxations via GABA-B agonism
classes.role_note: Selected specialist adjunct; sedation/dizziness and objective GERD confirmation are important.

classes.name: Antifoaming / gas-symptom adjunct
classes.mechanism: Reduces surface tension of gas bubbles without reducing acid secretion
classes.role_note: Symptom adjunct only; not an ulcer-healing or acid-suppression therapy.

labs.title: Pain, Analgesic & Muscle-Relaxant Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: PAIN MEDICINE / ANALGESIA / MUSCLE PHARMACOLOGY RESEARCH WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Nociceptive vs inflammatory vs neuropathic vs visceral pain → non-opioids → NSAIDs → opioids → adjuvants → local anesthetics → steroids → skeletal/smooth-muscle relaxants → anesthesia-only neuromuscular blockers
labs.scientific_boundary: Pain phenotype and diagnosis come before drug class. Steroids are anti-inflammatory pain-modifiers, muscle relaxants/antispasmodics do not directly equal analgesia, and neuromuscular blockers provide paralysis with NO analgesia/sedation. Opioids require individualized risk assessment; local anesthetic dose must be calculated as total mg for the exact procedure/product with LAST preparedness.

classification_notes.nonopioid: Paracetamol and NSAIDs are distinct non-opioid strategies. NSAIDs are especially useful for inflammatory pain but carry GI, renal and cardiovascular risk that rises with susceptibility, dose and duration.
classification_notes.opioid: CDC 2022 emphasizes individualized patient-centered decisions, preference for nonopioid therapy when appropriate, careful initiation/dose/duration decisions and harm-risk mitigation rather than rigid universal thresholds.
classification_notes.neuropathic: Neuropathic pain is mechanistically different from simple nociceptive pain; gabapentinoids, SNRIs, TCAs and sodium-channel agents are syndrome-specific adjuvants rather than universal analgesics.
classification_notes.local_anesthetic: Local anesthetics block voltage-gated sodium channels. Safe use is procedure- and concentration-specific; ASRA LAST readiness is a core safety concept.
classification_notes.muscle_relaxant: Acute skeletal muscle spasm, neurologic spasticity and visceral smooth-muscle spasm are different pharmacologic problems and should not share one undifferentiated “muscle relaxant” list.
classification_notes.nmb: Neuromuscular blockers are anesthesia/ICU paralytics only. They must never be represented as analgesics or sedatives.

classes.name: Paracetamol / acetaminophen
classes.mechanism: Central analgesic/antipyretic actions with weak peripheral anti-inflammatory activity; precise mechanism is multifactorial
classes.role_note: Foundational non-opioid analgesic/antipyretic; liver toxicity is dose-related.

classes.name: Salicylate analgesics
classes.mechanism: Irreversible or reversible cyclo-oxygenase inhibition depending agent/dose
classes.target: COX enzymes / platelet COX-1 for aspirin
classes.role_note: Aspirin has analgesic/anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet roles; dose and indication change pharmacology and safety.

classes.name: Propionic-acid NSAIDs
classes.mechanism: Reversible COX-1/COX-2 inhibition reduces prostaglandin synthesis
classes.role_note: Common NSAID family; GI/renal/CV risk varies by patient, dose and duration.

classes.name: Acetic-acid / related NSAIDs
classes.mechanism: COX inhibition with differing COX-1/COX-2 selectivity
classes.role_note: Includes diclofenac, indomethacin, ketorolac and related agents; potency does not remove class toxicity.

classes.name: Oxicam / enolic-acid NSAIDs
classes.mechanism: COX inhibition with long half-life for several members
classes.role_note: Long-acting NSAID family; prolonged exposure matters for GI/renal/CV toxicity.

classes.name: Selective / preferential COX-2 inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Preferential inhibition of COX-2-mediated inflammatory prostaglandins
classes.role_note: Less platelet COX-1 effect than nonselective NSAIDs but not free of CV/renal/GI risk.

classes.name: Topical NSAIDs
classes.mechanism: Local tissue COX inhibition with lower systemic exposure than oral therapy
classes.role_note: Useful local musculoskeletal pain category; systemic exposure is lower, not zero.

classes.name: Weak / atypical opioid analgesics
classes.mechanism: Opioid receptor agonism ± monoamine reuptake inhibition
classes.role_note: Opioid/monoaminergic agents with dependence, respiratory/CNS and serotonin/seizure risks.

classes.name: Full μ-opioid agonists
classes.mechanism: Activate μ-opioid receptors in brain, spinal cord and peripheral tissues
classes.role_note: Potent analgesics with dose-dependent respiratory depression, sedation, constipation, tolerance and dependence.

classes.name: Partial / mixed opioid receptor analgesics
classes.mechanism: Partial μ agonism or mixed κ/μ receptor pharmacology
classes.role_note: Distinct receptor pharmacology changes ceiling effects, withdrawal interactions and respiratory risk.

classes.name: Opioid antagonists / overdose rescue (not analgesics)
classes.mechanism: Competitively antagonize opioid receptors
classes.role_note: Safety/rescue category only; reverses opioid effects rather than treating pain.

classes.name: Gabapentinoid neuropathic-pain modulators
classes.mechanism: Bind α2δ subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels and reduce excitatory neurotransmitter release
classes.role_note: Neuropathic-pain/antiepileptic class; sedation, edema and renal dosing are high-yield.

classes.name: Sodium-channel anticonvulsants for neuralgia
classes.mechanism: Use-dependent blockade/stabilization of neuronal sodium channels
classes.role_note: Important for trigeminal neuralgia and selected neuropathic syndromes; not general nociceptive analgesics.

classes.name: SNRI analgesic adjuvants
classes.mechanism: Enhance descending serotonergic/noradrenergic pain inhibition
classes.role_note: Useful in neuropathic pain/fibromyalgia and selected chronic pain with comorbidity.

classes.name: Tricyclic antidepressant analgesic adjuvants
classes.mechanism: Enhance descending monoamine inhibition plus sodium-channel/anticholinergic effects
classes.role_note: Low-dose chronic neuropathic-pain category; anticholinergic/cardiac toxicity shapes patient selection.

classes.name: NMDA-antagonist analgesic/anesthetic adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Reduces central sensitization through NMDA receptor antagonism
classes.role_note: Ketamine is a monitored-setting analgesic/anesthetic adjunct; dissociation/hemodynamic/psychotomimetic effects require expertise.

classes.name: Central α2-adrenergic analgesic/sedative adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Reduces sympathetic outflow and modulates nociceptive transmission
classes.role_note: Analgesic-sparing sedative adjunct category in monitored settings.

classes.name: Amide local anesthetics
classes.mechanism: Block voltage-gated sodium channels from the intracellular side, preventing action-potential propagation
classes.role_note: Local/regional anesthesia class; total mg dose, vascularity, epinephrine, patient factors and LAST risk govern safe use.

classes.name: Ester local anesthetics
classes.mechanism: Block voltage-gated sodium channels; ester metabolism differs from amides
classes.role_note: Local anesthetic ester class; allergy/PABA and procedure-specific formulation issues are important.

classes.name: Topical non-NSAID analgesics
classes.mechanism: Peripheral nerve desensitization or sodium-channel blockade at local site
classes.role_note: Includes capsaicin and topical lidocaine; useful for localized pain with product-specific application limits.

classes.name: Triptans — migraine-specific acute antimigraine agents
classes.mechanism: 5-HT1B/1D agonism reduces trigeminovascular activation and cranial vasodilation
classes.role_note: Migraine-specific abortive class, not general analgesics; cardiovascular contraindications matter.

classes.name: CGRP receptor antagonists (gepants)
classes.mechanism: Block CGRP receptor signaling in trigeminovascular pathways
classes.role_note: Migraine-specific acute/preventive agents with less vasoconstriction than triptans; interactions vary.

classes.name: Systemic corticosteroids — anti-inflammatory pain-modifying agents (not primary analgesics)
classes.mechanism: Genomic glucocorticoid-receptor effects suppress inflammatory cytokines and immune activation
classes.role_note: Can reduce pain when inflammation is steroid-responsive; should not be classified as routine analgesics.

classes.name: Local/intra-articular corticosteroid preparations
classes.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory effects
classes.role_note: Procedure/diagnosis-specific anti-inflammatory injections; infection, tissue and glycemic risks matter.

classes.name: Centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxants for acute spasm
classes.mechanism: Reduce polysynaptic CNS motor activity through heterogeneous central mechanisms
classes.role_note: Short-term symptomatic category; sedation and limited duration are major practical issues.

classes.name: Antispasticity medicines
classes.mechanism: Reduce pathological UMN-mediated muscle tone through GABA/α2/peripheral calcium mechanisms
classes.role_note: For neurologic spasticity rather than simple muscle strain; titration/withdrawal and weakness monitoring are central.

classes.name: Botulinum toxin chemodenervation
classes.mechanism: Cleaves SNARE proteins and prevents acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junction
classes.role_note: Focal chemodenervation for selected spasticity/dystonia; units are product-specific and not interchangeable.

classes.name: Antimuscarinic smooth-muscle antispasmodics
classes.mechanism: Reduce muscarinic cholinergic contraction of GI smooth muscle
classes.role_note: Visceral-spasm symptom class; anticholinergic burden limits use in glaucoma, urinary retention and older adults.

classes.name: Direct / non-antimuscarinic smooth-muscle antispasmodics
classes.mechanism: Relax GI smooth muscle through phosphodiesterase/ion-channel/direct myotropic mechanisms
classes.role_note: Used in abdominal/visceral spasm in some markets; evidence and approval vary.

classes.name: Colchicine — anti-inflammatory crystal-arthritis agent (not analgesic)
classes.mechanism: Disrupts microtubules and neutrophil inflammasome-mediated inflammatory response
classes.role_note: Treats gout inflammation rather than directly blocking pain perception; narrow therapeutic index/interactions matter.

classes.name: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker — paralysis only
classes.mechanism: Persistent nicotinic ACh receptor depolarization causes neuromuscular paralysis
classes.role_note: Anesthesia/airway paralysis category. Provides NO analgesia, amnesia or sedation.

classes.name: Nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers — paralysis only
classes.mechanism: Competitive antagonism at nicotinic ACh receptors prevents neuromuscular transmission
classes.role_note: Anesthesia/ICU paralysis category. Provides NO analgesia or sedation and requires airway/ventilation plus neuromuscular monitoring.

labs.title: Respiratory & Allergy Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Asthma, COPD, allergic rhinitis, cough/mucus, severe-airway biologics and anaphylaxis pharmacology organized by mechanism and clinical context.
labs.scientific_boundary: Airway drugs are device-, phenotype-, severity- and diagnosis-dependent. Asthma controller therapy should include inhaled corticosteroid-containing treatment; bronchodilator monotherapy rules differ between asthma and COPD. Anaphylaxis requires prompt IM epinephrine; antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjuncts, not substitutes. Verify current inhaler strength/device technique, age, pregnancy, renal/hepatic context and regulatory label.

classification_notes.Controller_vs_relief: Separate anti-inflammatory control from bronchodilator symptom relief; combination products are not interchangeable by puff count.
classification_notes.Asthma_vs_COPD: LABA/LAMA use and ICS indications differ between asthma and COPD; never infer one disease algorithm from the other.
classification_notes.Inhaler_science: Particle delivery, inspiratory flow, spacer use, device technique and adherence can determine effectiveness as much as molecule choice.
classification_notes.Allergy_anaphylaxis: Rhinitis therapy is symptom-domain based; systemic anaphylaxis is an emergency and IM epinephrine is the core first-line drug.

classes.name: Short-acting β2 agonists (SABA)
classes.mechanism: Rapid β2-receptor stimulation increases airway smooth-muscle cAMP and bronchodilation
classes.role_note: Fast relievers for bronchospasm; in asthma, SABA-only treatment is not the preferred modern controller strategy.

classes.name: Long-acting β2 agonists (LABA)
classes.mechanism: Prolonged β2 stimulation maintains bronchodilation
classes.role_note: Maintenance bronchodilators. In asthma LABA should be paired with ICS; in COPD LABA may be used within bronchodilator-centered regimens.

classes.name: Short-acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA)
classes.mechanism: Blocks airway M3 muscarinic signaling and vagal bronchoconstriction
classes.role_note: Short-acting anticholinergic bronchodilation; often paired with SABA in acute COPD/asthma exacerbation settings.

classes.name: Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA)
classes.mechanism: Sustained M3 antagonism reduces cholinergic bronchoconstriction
classes.role_note: Core COPD maintenance class; tiotropium is also an add-on option in selected asthma contexts.

classes.name: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)
classes.mechanism: Glucocorticoid-receptor activation suppresses airway inflammatory gene expression
classes.role_note: Foundation of asthma anti-inflammatory treatment; COPD use is phenotype/exacerbation-context dependent and generally combined with long-acting bronchodilators.

classes.name: ICS–formoterol reliever / MART combinations
classes.mechanism: Combines airway anti-inflammatory corticosteroid with rapid-onset LABA bronchodilation
classes.role_note: Central modern asthma concept for selected products: same ICS-formoterol inhaler may be used as maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) or anti-inflammatory reliever according to step and product.

classes.name: Other ICS/LABA fixed combinations
classes.mechanism: Fixed anti-inflammatory controller plus long-acting bronchodilator
classes.role_note: Maintenance combinations; non-formoterol LABA products are not used as rapid reliever inhalers.

classes.name: ICS/LABA/LAMA triple inhalers
classes.mechanism: Combines anti-inflammatory ICS with dual long-acting bronchodilation
classes.target: Glucocorticoid receptor + β2 receptor + M3 receptor
classes.role_note: Escalation option in COPD and selected asthma products/contexts; phenotype and exacerbation history matter.

classes.name: Leukotriene receptor antagonists (LTRA)
classes.mechanism: Blocks cysteinyl-leukotriene receptor signaling
classes.role_note: Oral alternative/add-on in selected asthma/allergic rhinitis contexts; generally less effective than ICS for airway inflammation.

classes.name: Methylxanthines
classes.mechanism: Nonselective phosphodiesterase inhibition and adenosine antagonism increase bronchodilatory signaling
classes.role_note: Older narrow-therapeutic-index bronchodilator class; generally not preferred when safer inhaled options are available.

classes.name: PDE-4 pathway modifiers
classes.mechanism: Raises intracellular cAMP in inflammatory/airway cells via phosphodiesterase inhibition
classes.role_note: Selected COPD add-on therapy in exacerbation-prone/chronic-bronchitis phenotypes; newer inhaled PDE3/4 option may be used for maintenance bronchodilation.

classes.name: Systemic corticosteroids for airway exacerbations
classes.mechanism: Systemic glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory effects
classes.role_note: Short courses may be used for significant exacerbations; chronic systemic steroid exposure has substantial harm.

classes.name: Mucolytics / expectorants
classes.mechanism: Reduce mucus viscosity or facilitate secretion clearance
classes.role_note: Adjuncts for selected productive-cough/chronic-bronchitis contexts; they do not replace diagnosis-specific treatment.

classes.name: Antitussives
classes.mechanism: Suppress central cough reflex or peripheral cough receptors
classes.target: Medullary cough center / airway sensory pathways
classes.role_note: Symptom suppression only after red flags and underlying cause are considered; avoid masking serious disease.

classes.name: First-generation H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Inverse agonism at H1 receptors with substantial CNS penetration
classes.role_note: Effective antihistamines but sedation/anticholinergic burden limits routine daytime use.

classes.name: Second-generation H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Peripheral-selective H1 inverse agonism with less CNS penetration
classes.role_note: Preferred oral antihistamine family for many allergic rhinitis/urticaria contexts because of lower sedation burden.

classes.name: Intranasal H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Local nasal H1 blockade
classes.role_note: Rapid local symptom control, especially sneezing/rhinorrhea; can be combined with intranasal steroid in selected products.

classes.name: Intranasal corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid suppression of nasal inflammation
classes.role_note: Most effective monotherapy family for persistent allergic-rhinitis nasal symptoms when used correctly.

classes.name: Oral sympathomimetic decongestants
classes.mechanism: α-adrenergic vasoconstriction reduces nasal mucosal edema
classes.role_note: Short-term symptomatic congestion relief; cardiovascular/urinary/insomnia risk limits use.

classes.name: Topical nasal decongestants
classes.mechanism: Local α-adrenergic vasoconstriction
classes.role_note: Rapid short-term congestion relief; prolonged continuous use can cause rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa).

classes.name: Mast-cell stabilizer
classes.mechanism: Stabilizes mast cells and reduces mediator release
classes.role_note: Very safe preventive local therapy but requires regular use and is generally less potent than intranasal corticosteroids.

classes.name: Severe-asthma biologics
classes.mechanism: Target IgE or Type-2 cytokine signaling to reduce exacerbation biology
classes.role_note: Specialist phenotype-driven add-on therapy after diagnosis, adherence, inhaler technique and comorbidities are optimized.

classes.name: Epinephrine / adrenaline for anaphylaxis
classes.mechanism: α1 vasoconstriction + β1 cardiac support + β2 bronchodilation/mast-cell effects
classes.role_note: First-line emergency pharmacotherapy for anaphylaxis; give IM in the anterolateral thigh and repeat based on response/protocol.

classes.name: Allergen immunotherapy (SCIT / SLIT)
classes.mechanism: Repeated standardized allergen exposure induces immune tolerance
classes.role_note: Disease-modifying allergy treatment for selected sensitizations; requires diagnostic confirmation and specialist protocol.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult reliever: 1–2 inhalations as needed; acute regimens are severity/device specific.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Tremor, tachycardia, potassium with high-dose nebulization; reassess frequent use.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult nebulized regimen: 0.63–1.25 mg every 6–8 h when prescribed; device/indication specific.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Heart rate, tremor, paradoxical bronchospasm.

drugs.dose_example: Systemic dosing is indication- and region-specific; verify current product label.
drugs.role: Systemic β2 agonist; less preferred than inhaled route for routine airway relief.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Tachycardia, tremor, potassium/glucose; avoid routine substitution for inhaled therapy.

drugs.dose_example: Common maintenance component: 12 mcg twice daily as monotherapy product where indicated; combination/MART dosing is product specific.
drugs.role: Rapid-onset LABA used in maintenance and selected ICS-formoterol reliever strategies.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Do not use LABA monotherapy in asthma; monitor palpitations/tremor.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult maintenance: 50 mcg twice daily; verify product/indication.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not for acute relief; pair with ICS in asthma.

drugs.dose_example: Once-daily product strengths vary by country/device; verify label.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not rescue therapy; technique and cardiovascular symptoms.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult COPD maintenance: 5 mcg once daily via device-specific actuations.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not rescue therapy; device technique.

drugs.dose_example: Used only in fixed combinations; strength and once-daily regimen are product specific.
drugs.role: Ultra-LABA component of ICS/LABA or LABA/LAMA/triple products.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Do not prescribe as a standalone asthma LABA.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult inhaler maintenance/acute use is product and setting specific; nebulized 0.5 mg is a common acute dose.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Dry mouth; avoid ocular exposure from nebulized mask in glaucoma risk.

drugs.dose_example: Once-daily device-specific dosing; verify HandiHaler vs Respimat strength/indication.
drugs.role: Long-acting antimuscarinic; COPD core, selected asthma add-on.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Dry mouth, urinary retention, glaucoma caution; device-specific dosing.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult COPD maintenance: 62.5 mcg once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Anticholinergic adverse effects and inhaler technique.

drugs.dose_example: Product-dependent once/twice-daily dosing; verify formulation.
drugs.role: LAMA available alone and in combinations.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Dry mouth, urinary retention; do not equate inhaled and systemic dosing.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult COPD maintenance: 400 mcg twice daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Anticholinergic effects; inhaler technique.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult COPD maintenance: 175 mcg nebulized once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Anticholinergic effects; useful when handheld inhaler technique is difficult.

drugs.dose_example: Adult maintenance strengths vary; common total daily ranges are product/severity specific.
drugs.role: ICS with extensive asthma use; also in combinations.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Rinse mouth; oral candidiasis/dysphonia; assess cumulative steroid exposure.

drugs.dose_example: Device-specific microgram dosing; extrafine and conventional products are not dose-equivalent.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Rinse mouth; device/particle-size equivalence matters.

drugs.dose_example: Twice-daily strengths vary by severity/device; verify label.
drugs.role: Potent ICS used alone or in combinations.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Local candidiasis/dysphonia; systemic exposure at high doses.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult once-daily strengths 100 or 200 mcg depending indication/product.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Rinse mouth; not interchangeable mcg-for-mcg with fluticasone propionate.

drugs.dose_example: Once/twice-daily product-specific dosing; verify device.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Local steroid effects; technique.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult once/twice-daily microgram doses vary by market.
drugs.role: Prodrug ICS activated in lung tissue.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Rinse mouth; verify device strength.

drugs.dose_example: Maintenance/reliever puff limits are strength- and guideline-specific; verify the exact inhaler and GINA step.
drugs.role: Widely used ICS-formoterol combination for maintenance and selected reliever strategies.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Track total daily inhalations; confirm exact strength and maximum inhalations.

drugs.dose_example: MART/maintenance dosing is product-specific; verify label and local guideline.
drugs.role: ICS-formoterol combination with MART use in selected regions/products.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Device/strength-specific maximum daily use.

drugs.dose_example: Common maintenance: 1 inhalation twice daily; strength varies.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not rescue therapy; rinse mouth.

drugs.dose_example: Common maintenance: 1 inhalation once daily; strength/indication specific.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not acute relief; rinse mouth.

drugs.dose_example: Common maintenance: 2 inhalations twice daily; exact strength varies.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Rinse mouth; confirm whether product is approved for reliever use locally (often not).

drugs.dose_example: Common COPD maintenance: 1 inhalation once daily; asthma indication varies by market.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: ICS pneumonia/oral-thrush considerations in COPD; anticholinergic and LABA effects.

drugs.dose_example: Common COPD maintenance: 2 inhalations twice daily; verify exact strength.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not rescue therapy; rinse mouth and monitor anticholinergic/LABA effects.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 10 mg once daily.
drugs.role: LTRA used in asthma/allergic rhinitis and exercise-related bronchoconstriction contexts.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Neuropsychiatric warning; reassess benefit.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 20 mg twice daily on an empty stomach.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Liver injury and drug interactions; food affects absorption.

drugs.dose_example: Dose must be individualized to serum concentration, age, smoking, interactions and hepatic/cardiac status; do not use a fixed universal dose.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Serum level, arrhythmia/seizure toxicity, CYP interactions.

drugs.dose_example: Loading/infusion requires weight, prior theophylline exposure and serum-level calculation; specialist/acute-care verification required.
drugs.role: IV methylxanthine; limited role in modern acute airway care.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous ECG/levels; high interaction/toxicity burden.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 500 mcg once daily; some labels use 250 mcg lead-in.
drugs.role: PDE4 inhibitor for selected severe COPD with chronic bronchitis/exacerbations.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Weight loss, GI effects, mood symptoms; not a rescue bronchodilator.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult COPD maintenance: 3 mg nebulized twice daily where approved.
drugs.role: Inhaled dual PDE3/4 inhibitor for COPD maintenance.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Not rescue therapy; verify current local approval and label.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult exacerbation courses often use 40–50 mg daily for a short course; exact duration differs by asthma/COPD guideline.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose, mood, BP, infection; cumulative steroid burden.

drugs.dose_example: Acute-care dose is severity/route specific; verify protocol and equivalent glucocorticoid dose.
drugs.role: Systemic steroid option when oral/IV treatment is indicated.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Hyperglycemia, infection, psychiatric effects; IV is not automatically superior to oral.

drugs.dose_example: Common mucolytic adult regimens: 600 mg once or twice daily depending product/indication.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: GI effects; distinguish mucolytic use from acetaminophen-overdose protocols.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult initial total daily dose about 2.25 g divided, then reduced as response occurs; product-specific.
drugs.role: Mucoregulator used in some COPD/chronic sputum settings.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: GI effects; verify local availability.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult oral regimens vary by formulation (often 30 mg 2–3 times daily).
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Verify local label; rare severe skin reactions reported.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 8–16 mg three times daily depending product.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: GI effects; local label.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult ER: 600–1200 mg every 12 h, max product-specific.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Hydration and product combination ingredients.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult IR: 10–20 mg every 4 h or 30 mg every 6–8 h; max 120 mg/day in many labels.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Serotonergic interactions, misuse, combination-product duplication.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 100–200 mg three times daily as needed; swallow whole.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Fatal toxicity risk in children; do not chew/crush due oropharyngeal anesthesia.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult IR: 4 mg every 4–6 h; daily maximum product-specific.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Sedation, anticholinergic effects, driving/alcohol.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult allergy dose: 25–50 mg every 4–6 h; route/maximum varies.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Anticholinergic burden, falls/delirium in older adults; not first-line anaphylaxis treatment.

drugs.dose_example: Common pruritus/anxiety doses vary; use lowest effective dose.
drugs.role: Sedating H1 antihistamine with anxiolytic properties.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Sedation and QT risk; anticholinergic burden.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 10 mg once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Some sedation; renal dose adjustment.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 5 mg once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Renal adjustment; somnolence in some patients.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 10 mg once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Hepatic impairment may require adjustment.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 5 mg once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Generally low sedation; renal/hepatic context.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult allergic-rhinitis dose: 120 or 180 mg once daily depending indication/market.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Fruit juice/antacid absorption interactions; renal adjustment.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 20 mg once daily, usually fasting per label.
drugs.role: Non-sedating H1 antihistamine in many countries.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Food/fruit juice reduce absorption; verify local approval.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult use: 1–2 sprays per nostril twice daily depending product.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Bitter taste, somnolence in some patients; spray technique.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult use: 2 sprays per nostril twice daily depending product.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Epistaxis, bitter taste; technique.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start: 1–2 sprays per nostril once daily depending product.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Epistaxis; aim away from septum; use regularly.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult allergic-rhinitis dose: 2 sprays per nostril once daily.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Epistaxis/local irritation; technique.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 1–2 sprays per nostril once daily, product dependent.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Local irritation/epistaxis.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dose: 2 sprays per nostril once daily, reduce after control.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Local irritation/epistaxis.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult IR: 60 mg every 4–6 h; ER products vary; follow local maximum.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, tachycardia, insomnia, urinary retention; avoid uncontrolled hypertension.

drugs.dose_example: OTC strengths vary; clinical effectiveness of oral formulation is limited/controversial and regulatory status varies.
drugs.role: Systemic α1 decongestant in some OTC products.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP/heart rate; verify local regulatory status and effectiveness guidance.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult use: 2–3 sprays per nostril every 10–12 h for short duration; follow label.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Limit consecutive days; rebound congestion and systemic sympathomimetic effects.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult formulations: 0.1%, 1 spray per nostril up to 2–3 times/day for short duration.
drugs.role: Topical nasal decongestant used widely outside U.S.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Limit duration; rebound congestion.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult use: 1 spray per nostril 3–4 times daily; regular preventive use.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Frequent dosing; best before exposure; minimal systemic absorption.

drugs.dose_example: Dose and interval are determined by indication, pretreatment IgE and body weight; use dosing table.
drugs.role: Anti-IgE biologic for allergic asthma and other indications.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Anaphylaxis observation/education; IgE/weight eligibility.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult severe-asthma dose: 100 mg SC every 4 weeks.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Eosinophilic phenotype; hypersensitivity and helminth context.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult severe-asthma dose: 3 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Anaphylaxis risk; weight-based infusion.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult severe-asthma dose: 30 mg every 4 weeks for first 3 doses, then every 8 weeks.
drugs.role: Anti-IL-5 receptor biologic with eosinophil depletion.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Phenotype, hypersensitivity; do not abruptly stop steroids.

drugs.dose_example: Loading and maintenance depend on asthma/other indication; commonly every 2 weeks after loading.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Eosinophilia, conjunctivitis; steroid taper needs supervision.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult severe-asthma dose: 210 mg SC every 4 weeks.
drugs.role: Anti-TSLP biologic across broader severe-asthma phenotypes.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Hypersensitivity; phenotype/response reassessment.

drugs.dose_example: Adult anaphylaxis: 0.3–0.5 mg IM of 1 mg/mL solution, repeat every 5–15 min as needed per protocol; autoinjector strengths vary.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Airway, BP, oxygen, repeat dosing; IV bolus requires expert resuscitation context.

drugs.dose_example: Build-up and maintenance schedules are allergen/product-specific; no universal dose.
drugs.role: Specialist disease-modifying therapy for selected allergic disease.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Systemic reaction/anaphylaxis risk; post-injection observation.

drugs.dose_example: Daily product-specific dosing after supervised first dose for approved tablets.
drugs.role: Home maintenance immunotherapy after supervised initiation for selected allergens.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Oral reactions; anaphylaxis education; eosinophilic esophagitis contraindication for some products.

labs.title: Cardiovascular & Vascular Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: CARDIOLOGY • THROMBOSIS • LIPIDS • HEART FAILURE • ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY • VASCULAR MEDICINE
labs.subtitle: Antithrombotics → lipids → ischemia/ACS → heart failure → AF/arrhythmia → PAD/VTE → pulmonary vascular pharmacology → monitored emergency/advanced therapy
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. “Antiplatelet”, “anticoagulant”, “ACS”, “AF”, “HFrEF”, “PAD” and “PAH” tags describe pharmacologic/clinical contexts—not an automatic drug-of-choice recommendation. Verify diagnosis, ECG/EF, ischemic/bleeding risk, indication-specific dosing, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy, interactions, current guideline/label, local formulary and procedure/emergency protocol before prescribing. Fibrinolytics, IV antiarrhythmics, inotropes and PAH therapies require strict specialist/monitored workflows.

classification_notes.antiplatelet_vs_anticoagulant: Antiplatelets primarily inhibit platelet activation/aggregation and dominate arterial thrombosis/PCI pathways; anticoagulants inhibit the coagulation cascade and dominate AF/VTE/PE pathways. Combined therapy markedly increases bleeding and should be indication- and duration-specific.
classification_notes.acs_dapt: ACS/PCI antithrombotic therapy depends on reperfusion strategy, stent/procedure, ischemic vs bleeding risk and need for oral anticoagulation. The 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline is the primary contemporary reference in this lab.
classification_notes.af_stroke_prevention: AF management separates stroke prevention, rate control and rhythm control. Anticoagulation decisions use validated thromboembolic/bleeding risk assessment and valve/renal context; DOACs are not interchangeable with warfarin in every valvular/mechanical-valve setting.
classification_notes.hfrEF_four_pillars: Contemporary HFrEF foundational pharmacotherapy is organized around ARNI/RAAS inhibition, evidence-based beta blocker, MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor, with diuretics for congestion and additional therapies for selected phenotypes.
classification_notes.lipids_2026: The 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline restores explicit LDL/non-HDL goals and emphasizes earlier, risk-based intensification using statins plus evidence-based nonstatin therapies when needed.
classification_notes.pad_vascular: PAD treatment is systemic ASCVD therapy plus limb-specific care: antithrombotic strategy, intensive lipid lowering, smoking cessation/exercise and revascularization assessment. Claudication drugs are symptom modifiers, not substitutes for vascular risk reduction.
classification_notes.vte_pe: Acute PE/VTE requires severity/risk stratification. The 2026 AHA/ACC acute PE guideline generally favors DOACs over VKAs for eligible oral-anticoagulation patients and LMWH over UFH when initial parenteral therapy is needed, unless clinical factors dictate otherwise.
classification_notes.antiarrhythmics: Vaughan-Williams classes are useful for mechanism learning but do not by themselves determine safe drug selection. Structural heart disease, EF, QT, renal function, conduction disease, ischemia and interacting drugs can completely change the appropriate choice.
classification_notes.pulmonary_vascular: PAH drugs must not be started merely because “pulmonary hypertension” appears on an echo. Confirm PH group/hemodynamics and specialist indication; therapies for group 1 PAH/CTEPH are not routine treatment for left-heart or hypoxic lung-disease PH.

classes.name: Aspirin / COX-1 antiplatelet
classes.mechanism: Irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1, reducing thromboxane A2
classes.role_note: Foundational antiplatelet in many atherosclerotic contexts; indication and bleeding risk determine use.

classes.name: P2Y12 receptor inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibit ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation
classes.role_note: Core DAPT partners after ACS/PCI; choice depends on ACS strategy, bleeding, stroke history and interactions.

classes.name: GPIIb/IIIa inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Block final common platelet aggregation pathway by inhibiting fibrinogen binding
classes.role_note: Selective cath-lab/PCI use rather than routine outpatient antiplatelet therapy.

classes.name: Direct oral factor-Xa inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Directly inhibit activated factor X and thrombin generation
classes.role_note: Major oral anticoagulant class for AF and VTE when appropriate; indication-specific dosing is essential.

classes.name: Direct thrombin inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Directly inhibit thrombin (factor IIa)
classes.role_note: Includes oral dabigatran and parenteral agents used in PCI/HIT contexts.

classes.name: Vitamin-K antagonists
classes.mechanism: Reduce hepatic synthesis of vitamin-K–dependent clotting factors
classes.role_note: Still essential in mechanical valves and selected valvular/thrombophilic contexts; requires INR-guided dosing.

classes.name: Heparins (UFH / LMWH)
classes.mechanism: Potentiate antithrombin-mediated inhibition of factor Xa and/or thrombin
classes.role_note: Hospital and bridging anticoagulation class; LMWH and UFH differ in kinetics/monitoring.

classes.name: Indirect factor-Xa inhibitor (fondaparinux)
classes.mechanism: Synthetic pentasaccharide potentiates antithrombin inhibition of Xa
classes.role_note: Once-daily parenteral anticoagulant with weight/renal considerations.

classes.name: Fibrinolytic / thrombolytic agents
classes.mechanism: Convert plasminogen to plasmin and promote fibrin clot dissolution
classes.role_note: Time-critical emergency reperfusion drugs; indication, contraindication and protocol verification are mandatory.

classes.name: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins)
classes.mechanism: Reduce hepatic cholesterol synthesis and upregulate LDL receptors
classes.role_note: Foundation LDL-lowering therapy across ASCVD risk categories; intensity and target depend on risk.

classes.name: Cholesterol absorption inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Blocks intestinal NPC1L1-mediated cholesterol absorption
classes.role_note: Common first add-on to statin when further LDL lowering is needed.

classes.name: PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies
classes.mechanism: Prevent PCSK9-mediated LDL-receptor degradation
classes.role_note: Potent LDL lowering for high-risk ASCVD/familial hypercholesterolemia when indicated.

classes.name: PCSK9 siRNA therapy
classes.mechanism: Silences hepatic PCSK9 synthesis via RNA interference
classes.role_note: Twice-yearly maintenance LDL-lowering option after initial and 3-month doses.

classes.name: ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Inhibits hepatic cholesterol synthesis upstream of HMG-CoA reductase
classes.role_note: Oral nonstatin LDL-lowering option, including selected statin-intolerant patients.

classes.name: Fibrates (PPAR-α agonists)
classes.mechanism: Increase fatty-acid oxidation and reduce triglyceride-rich lipoproteins
classes.role_note: Primarily triglyceride-focused agents; role depends on TG severity and overall risk.

classes.name: Prescription omega-3 / EPA therapy
classes.mechanism: Reduces hepatic VLDL-triglyceride production and alters lipid metabolism
classes.role_note: Selected high-TG and cardiovascular-risk contexts; prescription products differ from supplements.

classes.name: Bile-acid sequestrants
classes.mechanism: Bind intestinal bile acids and increase hepatic LDL-receptor activity
classes.role_note: Older oral LDL-lowering class; can worsen triglycerides and interfere with drug absorption.

classes.name: Organic nitrates
classes.mechanism: Generate nitric oxide, increasing cGMP and reducing preload/ischemia
classes.role_note: Symptom-relief/acute anti-ischemic vasodilators; nitrate-free interval needed for chronic formulations.

classes.name: β-blockers for ischemia/rate control
classes.mechanism: Block cardiac β-adrenergic signaling, lowering heart rate and contractility
classes.role_note: High-value class when there is a compelling indication such as angina, prior MI, arrhythmia or HFrEF.

classes.name: Calcium-channel blockers for angina/rate control
classes.mechanism: Reduce L-type calcium entry in vascular smooth muscle and/or AV node
classes.role_note: DHP agents mainly vasodilate; non-DHP agents also slow AV conduction and need EF/conduction review.

classes.name: Other antianginal / metabolic agents
classes.mechanism: Reduce ischemia through late-Na inhibition, K-channel effects or metabolic mechanisms
classes.role_note: Adjunct antianginal options when symptoms persist or standard agents are limited; approvals vary by country.

classes.name: ARNI / RAAS inhibition in HFrEF
classes.mechanism: Reduces RAAS signaling; ARNI also augments natriuretic peptide pathways
classes.role_note: Foundational HFrEF pathway; ARNI is preferred for many symptomatic HFrEF patients when tolerated.

classes.name: Evidence-based β-blockers in HFrEF
classes.mechanism: Blunt chronic sympathetic activation and improve ventricular remodeling
classes.role_note: Use one of the evidence-based β-blockers and titrate when clinically stable/euvolemic.

classes.name: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
classes.mechanism: Block aldosterone effects, reducing sodium retention and fibrosis
classes.role_note: Foundational HFrEF class when potassium/renal criteria are met.

classes.name: SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure
classes.mechanism: Promote glycosuria/natriuresis and favorable cardiorenal physiology
classes.role_note: Foundational HFrEF therapy and useful across a broad EF spectrum independent of diabetes status when indicated.

classes.name: Loop diuretics for congestion
classes.mechanism: Block NKCC2 in thick ascending limb, causing potent natriuresis
classes.role_note: Relieve congestion/symptoms; dose is individualized to prior exposure, renal function and diuretic response.

classes.name: Sequential nephron blockade adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Add distal sodium-chloride blockade to loop diuretics
classes.role_note: Short-term adjunct for diuretic resistance; high electrolyte/renal monitoring burden.

classes.name: Hydralazine + nitrate vasodilator therapy
classes.mechanism: Arterial dilation plus venodilation reduces afterload and preload
classes.role_note: HFrEF add-on or alternative in selected patients; fixed-dose combination evidence exists.

classes.name: Cardiac glycoside
classes.mechanism: Inhibits Na/K ATPase and increases vagal tone
classes.role_note: Narrow-therapeutic-index adjunct for selected HFrEF/AF patients; not a routine first-line rate-control drug for everyone.

classes.name: If-channel inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Selectively slows sinus-node pacemaker current without reducing contractility
classes.role_note: Selected symptomatic HFrEF patients in sinus rhythm with elevated HR despite maximally tolerated β-blocker.

classes.name: Soluble guanylate-cyclase stimulator
classes.mechanism: Stimulates sGC and increases cGMP signaling
classes.role_note: Selected high-risk HFrEF after recent worsening HF despite guideline-directed therapy.

classes.name: IV inotropes / inodilators
classes.mechanism: Increase contractility via β-adrenergic signaling or PDE3 inhibition
classes.role_note: Monitored short-term therapy for selected low-output/shock/advanced HF; not routine chronic outpatient treatment.

classes.name: Class IA antiarrhythmics
classes.mechanism: Moderate fast-Na block plus repolarization effects
classes.role_note: Specialist rhythm-control agents with important QT/proarrhythmia limitations.

classes.name: Class IB antiarrhythmics
classes.mechanism: Fast-Na channel block with preference for ischemic/depolarized ventricular tissue
classes.role_note: Primarily ventricular arrhythmia role; lidocaine is IV, mexiletine oral.

classes.name: Class IC antiarrhythmics
classes.mechanism: Potent fast-Na channel block with marked conduction slowing
classes.role_note: Selected AF/SVT rhythm control in patients without significant structural/ischemic heart disease.

classes.name: Class III antiarrhythmics
classes.mechanism: Predominantly prolong repolarization via potassium-channel effects; some have mixed actions
classes.role_note: Potent rhythm-control class with agent-specific organ/QT monitoring and inpatient initiation requirements for some drugs.

classes.name: Non-DHP CCBs for AV-nodal rate control
classes.mechanism: Slow AV-nodal conduction through L-type calcium-channel blockade
classes.role_note: Rate-control class for selected AF/SVT patients; avoid in significant HFrEF.

classes.name: Adenosine
classes.mechanism: Transiently activates A1 receptors and blocks AV-nodal conduction
classes.role_note: Very short-acting diagnostic/therapeutic drug for regular narrow-complex AV-node–dependent SVT.

classes.name: PAD claudication symptom agents
classes.mechanism: Improve walking symptoms via PDE3 inhibition or hemorheologic effects
classes.role_note: Symptom-directed PAD agents do not replace antiplatelet, statin, exercise, smoking cessation and revascularization assessment.

classes.name: PDE5 inhibitors for pulmonary arterial hypertension
classes.mechanism: Increase cGMP by inhibiting phosphodiesterase-5 in pulmonary vasculature
classes.role_note: PAH-specific therapy requiring accurate PH classification; not interchangeable with routine systemic hypertension treatment.

classes.name: Endothelin-receptor antagonists
classes.mechanism: Block endothelin-mediated pulmonary vasoconstriction/remodeling
classes.role_note: PAH disease-targeted class with pregnancy and liver/hematology precautions.

classes.name: Prostacyclin-pathway therapies
